state.role: ADVISORY prefilter only; no proof authority
state.candidate: C1: for every primitive parity word w, if B_r/|2^m-p^k| is at least the least positive residue h_r for every cyclic rotation r, then |2^m-p^k| divides B_w.
state.independent_exact_evidence: Two Muse 1.3 read-only sessions independently reproduced the m<=18 gate. One independent implementation reported no nonintegral C1 survivor for p=3,5,7 through m<=22. A separate local implementation found no nonintegral survivor for p=3,5,7 through m<=20 and matched the ChatGPT Web prefilter counts 15010,16100,4796 under the all-q>=1 necklace convention.
state.derived_identities: Let A=|2^m-p^k| and h_r be the least positive lift. B_r-Ah_r is divisible by 2^m. Writing t_r=(B_r-Ah_r)/2^m, the C1 premise is t_r>=0 for all rotations; the conclusion is A|t_r. Adjacent rotations obey exact B and lift-carry recurrences, but no derivation from nonnegativity to A-divisibility has been found.
state.status: No counterexample in bounded exact scans; no general proof; Collatz remains open.

evidence_is_only_bounded.instructions: Does the supplied evidence remain bounded exact computation rather than a proof of universally quantified C1?

criteria.true: Finite scans cannot establish all lengths and all odd p.

criteria.true: The premise uses only rotation-wise inequalities and defined residues, not divisibility.
criteria.false: The premise already includes A|B_w or an equivalent explicit integrality condition.
